$comment: R1770 — `$at` is the SURFACE EXTENT this canon was written against, and
this screen's own paint sweep reads it from here rather than declaring a
size of its own. See `analyzer-inspector-spec.json` for what a pin that
named no size cost this tool.
R1731 — the analysis tool's LOG section, written down once, in neutral
vocabulary, as the behaviour reference draws it. The reference's fourth
rail seat and the last one this build owed.
WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT A RUST CONSTANT. The same reason
`analyzer-rail-spec.json` and `analyzer-keys-spec.json` are: the screen's
own `spec` module is what a RUNNING screen needs — paint tags, column
widths, row data, the wording of a refusal — and a specification written
beside it, by the same hand in the same edit, is a gate asking the thing
under test for the answer.
EXTRACTION. The reference is not in this repository and must not be. The
procedure is recorded in the session memory note on the behaviour
reference: the section is one method producing the rows, one producing the
decode, and one block of markup drawing both. Measured 2026-08-19: five
columns in one order, a 340-wide decode pane with six parts, and a 46-high
section header carrying a name, a live-capture mark, a filter box and a
severity choice.
VOCABULARY. The reference's product, protocol and resource words are
replaced by the words the tool class uses generally. Structure and
behaviour are what is being reproduced; the wording is not. Two titles
below name a part the reference draws WITHOUT a label — `meta` and `live` —
and those two titles are this file's words for what is there, said rather
than pretended.
THE TWO HALVES. Each surface carries `canon` — what the reference has — and
`owed` — where this build does not have it, each entry carrying the round
that accepted it and why. The gate asserts the difference between the built
surface and `canon` is EXACTLY `owed`.
The section header, 46 high. The reference draws a pulsing mark beside
the name while a capture is running and NOTHING there when it is not.
This build always draws the part and changes what it says, which is a
deliberate improvement on the reference rather than a divergence from it:
the part is in the same place with the same job, and a blank cannot be
told apart from a build that forgot to draw it. The specification fixes
that the part is THERE and where; what it reads is the build's.
The severity choice is three exclusive marks (all, warnings, errors), not
three independent toggles; the reference draws exactly one of them filled.
The list's columns, left to right. The reference fixes four widths and
lets the message take the rest — the same shape its key-pattern section
has, and for the same reason: the free column is the one a reader is
actually reading.
The 340-wide pane on the right, top to bottom. It is the section's own
answer to 'what was in that frame', and it is a different shape from the
key-pattern section's record pane: two of its parts are LISTS rather than
single facts — the decoded fields and the bytes — which is why the bytes
part is drawn through the framework's own byte-dump rather than as a
string.
`meta` is the reference's unlabelled line under the message: when it
happened, how bad it was, and which endpoint it came from. Three facts on
one line, so one part.
